Dan Osborn

By Petition candidate for United States Senator, Nebraska · Challenger

Industrial mechanic and former union leader; Navy veteran

Dan Osborn is a registered nonpartisan Navy veteran and former Omaha union leader. He ran for U.S. Senate in 2024 and lost to Republican Sen. Deb Fischer by about six percentage points. He is now running by petition against incumbent Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Osborn stands

Tariffs and trade
Supports targeted tariffs, citing protection for the U.S. auto industry. Says blanket tariffs raise costs for small businesses and families, including building materials and the cost of buying a home.
Beef prices and agriculture
Opposes the administration's expansion of tariff-free beef imports, including Argentina's quota. Says the President "needs to scrap this deal" because it undercuts American cattle producers.
Social Security and Medicare
Proposes raising or changing the income cap on Social Security payroll taxes to strengthen the program, saying higher earners should pay a fairer share.
Congressional stock trading
Supports banning individual stock trading by members of Congress and the executive branch. Says members who trade on insider information should go to jail.
Party donor disclosure
Calls dark money in elections a "big problem" that needs fixing and pledges not to leave his door open to special interests. In a debate, he acknowledged that outside groups backing him have taken money from undisclosed donors.
Party caucus
Says that if elected he would not caucus with either the Republican or the Democratic party.
Health insurance subsidies
Said he would have fought to extend the health insurance premium tax credits at the center of the 2025 federal shutdown fight.
